old_text: A match is played between two sides of eleven players each, unless otherwise agreed to; each side has two innings, taken alternately, except in the case provided for in Law 54.
new_text: A match is played between two sides of eleven players each, unless otherwise agreed to; each side has two innings, taken alternately, except in the case provided for in Law 53.

old_text: No match is won unless played out or given up, except in the case provided for in Law 45.

old_text: Before the commencement of the match two umpires shall be appointed, one for each end.
new_text: Before the commencemen of the match two umpires shall be appointed, one for each end.

old_text: The ball shall weigh not less than 5½oz., nor more than 5¾oz.
new_text: The ball shall weigh no less than 5½oz., nor more than 5¾oz.

old_text: It shall measure not less than 9in. nor more than 9¼in. in circumference.

old_text: At the beginning of each innings either side may demand a new ball. ii.

old_text: The bails shall be each 4¾in. in length, and when in position, on the top of the stumps, shall not project more than ¾in. above them.
new_text: The bails shall be each 4½in. in length, and when in position, on the top of the stumps, shall not project more than ¾in. above them.

old_text: The ground shall not be rolled, watered, covered, mown or beaten during a match, except before the commencement of each innings and of each day’s play, when, unless the in-side object, the ground shall be swept and rolled for not more than ten minutes.
new_text: The ground shall not be rolled, watered, covered, mown or beaten during a match, except before the commencement of each innings and of each day’s play; when, unless the in-side object, the ground shall be swept and rolled for not more than ten minutes.

old_text: This shall not prevent the batsman from beating the ground with his bat, nor the batsman nor bowler from using sawdust in order to obtain a proper foothold.
new_text: This shall not prevent the batsmen from beating the ground with his bat, nor the batsman or bowler from using sawdust in order to obtain a proper foothold.

old_text: The ball must be bowled; if thrown or jerked, the umpire shall call “No ball.” iii.
new_text: The ball must be bowled; if thrown or jerked, the umpire shall call "No-ball.”

old_text: The bowler shall deliver the ball with one foot on the ground behind the bowling crease, and within the return crease, otherwise the umpire shall call “No-Ball.”
new_text: The bowler shall deliver the ball with one foot on the ground behind the bowling crease and within the return crease, otherwise the umpire shall call "No ball.”

old_text: The ball shall be bowled in overs of four balls from each wicket alternately.
new_text: The ball shall be bowled in overs of five balls from each wicket alternately.

old_text: When four balls have been bowled, and the ball is finally settled in the bowler’s or wicket-keeper’s hands, the umpire shall call “Over.”
new_text: When five balls have been bowled, and the ball is finally settled in the bowler’s or wicket-keeper’s hands, the umpire shall call "Over."

new_text: Neither a "No-ball" nor a "Wide-ball” shall be reckoned as one of the “Over."

old_text: The bowler may not change ends more than twice in the same innings nor bowl more than two overs in succession.
new_text: The bowler shall be allowed to change ends as often as he pleases, provided only that he does not bowl two overs consecutively in one innings.

new_text: The striker may hit a "no ball," and whatever runs result shall be added to his score; but he shall not be out from a "noball,” unless he be run out or break Laws 26, 27, 29, 30.

old_text: From a “ wide ball ” as many runs as are run shall be added to the score as “ wide balls,” and if no run be otherwise obtained one run shall be so added. iv.
new_text: From a wide ball as many runs as are run shall be added to the score as "wide balls,” and if no run be otherwise obtained one run shall be so added.

old_text: If the ball, not having been called “ wide ” or “no-ball,” pass the striker, without touching his bat, or person, and any runs be obtained, the umpire shall call “bye;” but if the ball touch any part of the striker’s person (hand excepted) and any run be obtained, the umpire shall call “leg-bye,” such runs to be scored “byes” and “ leg-byes” respectively.

old_text: At the beginning of the match, and of each innings, the umpire at the bowler’s wicket shall call “Play”; from that time no trial ball shall be allowed to any bowler on the ground between the wickets, and when one of the batsmen is out the use of the bat shall not be allowed to any person until the next batsman shall come in.
